A page and its CDN now go one way: on networks where the cut works for only some of a service's media hosts, the player no longer goes direct while its new hosts go through the tunnel and get refused. A change of network is seen in seconds, and a block by name is called only when it holds pass after pass.

To update, run the new `dpiswitch.exe` from anywhere and accept the offer to install over the installed version (one administrator prompt). Settings, lists, configs and verdicts are kept.

## Detector and routes

- **CDN families.** A media URL is signed for the address its page came from. A CDN is tied to its page by the CDN's own certificate (googlevideo.com names `*.c.youtube.com`, a zone of youtube.com), and the two go the tunnel's way together until 1 in 4 of the CDN's names checked (10 at least) go direct and no page is blocked; direct, they keep so down to 15 in 100. A family stands only once one of its pages has a verdict on this network. When a family changes its way, its connections going the old one are closed; the user's own lists are left alone. A CDN host sent direct by its family is checked like an inherited one, and a name dropped from the UI counts as not passed until checked again.
- **Refusal.** Through the tunnel the service refuses a CDN host (a 403 for the tunnel's address). Only a family's CDN hosts are refused, only while their family goes direct, and only at 1 in 4 direct or more -- below it the blocked keep the tunnel. A host blocked on both direct ways whose domain goes direct at 3 in 4 is refused, so the player takes another host at once instead of waiting.
- **A block by name is confirmed.** One failed pass made a block: a node answering one time in two was called BLOCKED_DPI and refused. Three more passes now, direct with the name, direct without it and through the tunnel; a block by name fails with the name and gets through without it on most passes, failing both ways is the address (BLOCKED_TCP), anything else INCONCLUSIVE. A pass that failed by a fluke while every confirming one got through is made again, once.
- **A change of network is seen in seconds**, not a minute: the adapters and their addresses are watched every 2 s, the public address every 30 s (the one sign of a router's uplink switched behind the same gateway), and the UI shows the new network at once. The connections the detector's lists routed are closed on the change, so a site does not keep the old network's way.
- Link-local addresses are left out of the local network: Bluetooth's and Wi-Fi Direct's adapters come and go.

## Interface

- BLOCKED_TCP reads "blocked by address".
- Verdicts: a click on a column's head sorts by it; by name by default.
- Settings: every row in a line or two, its name a link to its part of the help. "Cut the ClientHello" and "QUIC decoy" are two switches again; switching the decoy needs no core restart.
- Live: fixed column widths, rows 27 px, the time of each event; rows keep their order while the cursor is over the table; the table keeps its length while rows are picked.
- Row menu: the address of every row, this program's own file for the detector's checks, File location greyed for several rows.

## Presets

- Telegram takes in WhatsApp (a preset switched on stays on); Discord is new.
- AI services: duplicate entries removed.

Core: the fork's 8067c742 (mihomo Alpha 9f053c49).
